scope: Practical app color and typography guidance. WCAG thresholds are requirements; layout, font pairings, and token advice are design recommendations, not a conformance certification.

sources.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Dark Mode
Google Fonts official font sources and OFL licenses

thresholds.label: AA normal text
thresholds.guidance: Use at least 4.5:1 for body text, UI labels, input text, and placeholders.

thresholds.label: AA large text
thresholds.guidance: At least 3:1 applies only at 24 CSS px regular, or about 18.67 CSS px bold, and larger. Keep 4.5:1 as the practical default.

thresholds.label: AAA normal text
thresholds.guidance: At least 7:1 is the enhanced target for normal text; large text needs 4.5:1.

thresholds.label: Essential controls and graphics
thresholds.guidance: Essential control boundaries, states, icons, and graphical information need 3:1 against adjacent colors. Decorative separators and every card edge do not automatically need 3:1.

contrast_notes: Contrast is a relationship between two colors, never a property of a swatch alone.
Classify with the unrounded computed ratio. A displayed value of 4.50 may still fail if the actual ratio is below 4.5.
Ratios calculated for solid opaque sRGB hex colors do not certify translucent overlays, gradients, images, or the final app.
For opacity, composite the actual foreground and background first; evaluate the final displayed pair.
For gradients and images, test the weakest area behind text. A solid text container is easier to validate.
Inactive controls are exempt from text contrast thresholds, but keep their purpose readable and explain why unavailable. Placeholder text is not a substitute for a persistent label.
A pass does not guarantee comfortable reading: very thin strokes, small type, glare, and rendering still matter.

focus_and_color.text: Keyboard focus must be visible (2.4.7 AA), and the focused component must not be entirely hidden by authored content (2.4.11 AA).
Color must not be the only visual signal. Add words, icons, patterns, position, or underlines to communicate state and meaning.
Use a solid 2–3 px focus outline with an offset and a contrasting inner/outer halo when backgrounds vary. Verify the indicator against every adjacent surface.

2.4.13 Focus Appearance requires indicator area at least equivalent to a 2 CSS px perimeter, and a 3:1 change between the same pixels when focused versus unfocused, subject to its exceptions. This is AAA, not AA.
Underline inline links persistently. Pair errors with an icon, message, and field association. Pair selection with a checkmark or shape change.

theme_rules: Name colors by role in product code: canvas, surface, raised, text, muted, border, primary, onPrimary, focus, success, warning, error, info.
Keep original palette hex values as primitives; map semantic roles separately in Light and Dark modes.
Do not mechanically invert hex colors. Dark mode usually uses darker surfaces and lighter text or accents, with separate state values.
Use one color family as the foundation, one restrained accent, and separate semantic status colors. An accent is not automatically safe for text.
Pair each colored fill with its matching on-color token. A pale dark-mode primary button usually needs dark label text.
Evaluate text on canvas, surface, raised surface, selected surface, hover, and pressed states separately.
Distinguish decorative dividers from essential input borders. A subtle border can decorate a card but must not be the only signal identifying an input.
Keep status meaning consistent across appearances; adapt the lightness of the color, not the meaning.
Use lighter surfaces or a border to separate raised dark surfaces where shadows disappear. Avoid flooding all surfaces with the brand hue.
Respect platform appearance and increased-contrast preferences. Validate in bright and dim environments, on real displays.
Give links, disabled states, focus, selected controls, errors, charts, overlays, and image treatments explicit tokens before shipping.
Use any palette personality or product-category suggestion as creative direction, not a universal psychological fact.
chart_rules: Categorical data: distinct hues plus direct labels and shapes. Do not use the six shades of one family for unrelated categories.
Sequential data: order a single-hue ramp by measured luminance; communicate direction with labels or a legend.
Diverging data: two hues around a meaningful midpoint; do not imply a midpoint where none exists.
Use line dashes, point shapes, textures, and text so hue is never the sole key. Avoid relying on red versus green.
Check essential marks against their background and adjacent marks. Separators or outlines can clarify boundaries.
Keep label text contrast separate from chart-mark contrast. Include a written takeaway and an accessible data table.
Test color-vision simulations and grayscale as additional checks; they do not replace accessible names or keyboard support.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.pairing: Inter alone; optionally add IBM Plex Mono for code and hex values
fonts.fallback: Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif
fonts.basis: Designed for computer screens; variable family with useful numeric features.

fonts.name: Manrope
fonts.role: Friendly geometric headings and short UI copy
fonts.pairing: Manrope headings + Inter body; or Manrope alone for a compact identity
fonts.basis: A geometric and grotesque blend with semi-rounded forms. Choice of product fit is editorial.
fonts.license_note: This guide bundles Google Fonts Manrope 4.505 under OFL 1.1. The current designer release V5 has different terms; do not mix versions or assume identical files.

fonts.name: Source Serif 4
fonts.role: Editorial headings, reading content, premium storytelling
fonts.pairing: Source Serif 4 headings + Inter UI; Source Serif 4 reading text + Inter controls
fonts.basis: Optical sizes and Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic coverage; use text optical sizes for reading and display sizes for large headings.
fonts.license_note: Official release uses SIL Open Font License 1.1; keep the license with redistributed fonts.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Sans
fonts.role: Technical product UI, labels, tables and dashboard content
fonts.pairing: IBM Plex Sans UI + IBM Plex Mono for code and technical labels
fonts.fallback: IBM Plex Sans, Inter, system-ui, sans-serif
fonts.basis: Part of the coordinated IBM Plex superfamily; product-category fit is an editorial recommendation.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Mono
fonts.role: Code, hex values, IDs, compact numeric annotations
fonts.recommended_for: Developer tools and technical reference labels
fonts.pairing: Inter UI + IBM Plex Mono detail
fonts.fallback: IBM Plex Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
fonts.basis: IBM's monospaced family fits glyphs to equal advance widths; use sparingly for dense prose.

fonts.name: Noto Sans / Noto Sans Bengali
fonts.recommended_for: Localized applications with script-specific fallback needs
fonts.pairing: Noto Sans for Latin and Noto Sans Bengali for Bangla content
fonts.fallback: Noto Sans Bengali, Noto Sans, system-ui, sans-serif
fonts.basis: Choose the correct Noto family per script. Validate real translated strings, shaping, numerals, line heights, and clipping; glyph coverage is not proof of layout quality.

typography_notes: This scale is a starting recommendation, not a WCAG minimum font-size rule. Use scalable units in implementation and support platform text sizing.
Use 16–18 px for sustained reading, 1.45–1.6 line height, and roughly 45–75 characters per line as starting design targets.
Use 400–600 for normal UI; avoid ultra-light body text. Test mixed scripts and real device rendering.
Keep captions for secondary metadata. Never shrink essential instructions to make a layout fit.
Use tabular numerals for tables and aligned metrics; do not force all body text into monospace.
Limit an app to one main family plus one purposeful companion. Use spacing, size, and weight for hierarchy before adding families.
Install the exact family and weights used by the design. Verify fallback metrics and retain license files in implementation.
release_checklist: Check every actual text/background token pair in both themes using unrounded ratios.
Inspect default, hover, pressed, focused, selected, error, success, loading, and disabled states.
Check focus against all surfaces and ensure it remains visible while scrolling.
Check status meaning without color and chart meaning without hue.
Check translucency, overlays, gradients, images, and composited colors at their weakest point.
Test text enlargement, fallback fonts, translated strings, clipping, and line wrapping.
Check high contrast or forced-color modes and platform appearance preference behavior.
Inspect on real devices in bright and dim environments. Recheck after any token or opacity change.
font_bundle_note: Fonts live in work/fonts for authoring; no global installation. All five downloaded or copied files are valid TrueType fonts. Their OFL text and source manifest accompany the files. Noto Bengali is a suggested fallback and is not bundled.
